texts: good. the bare-plural generic becomes a fireable rule giving each Keeper his own coat, and both "long" and the oilcloth kind are carried.
good. the definite plural gets both the group-level claim and a per-coat rule, and "against sea-spray" is kept exactly as written.

bad: it is recorded as one particular essence staining one particular coat rather than as the general truth about Keepers' coats, so nothing follows for any other Keeper, and "over time" has no representation at all and is silently dropped. Make the generality explicit with a universal, which is the only edit needed: "Mire-essence stains every Keeper's coat." If the gradualness matters, say it in a second sentence as a span with a stated figure ("a coat is stained after ten years of wear"), because a bare "over time" or "gradually" cannot be recorded at all.
good. the first-year apprentice is typed as a kind of apprentice and "unstained" is kept as a plain property of the coat, with the one-off wearing correctly not turned into a rule.
